title: While Loops
intro: Iteration Structures: Conditions and Boolean Flags
bullets: Check a condition before each iteration.
Repeat until a stopping condition is met.
Use a Boolean flag to control a loop.

title: How a while Loop Works
paragraphs: A while loop repeats a block of code when its condition is True.
Python checks the condition before each iteration.
A True condition starts the next iteration. A False condition ends the loop.
The program then continues with the first instruction after the loop.

title: Changing the Condition
paragraphs: The loop runs while count < 5 is True. Each iteration displays count and increases it by 1.
When count reaches 5, the condition is False. The loop finishes.

title: A Loop Can Be Skipped
paragraphs: The condition is checked before the body runs.
Here, count starts at 5. The condition count < 5 is already False.
The loop body does not run. The final print still runs.
code:
count = 5

while count < 5:
    print(count)
    count += 1

print("Loop complete.")

title: Repeating Until a Response Is Received
paragraphs: The loop keeps asking while answer is not yes.
Each response replaces the value stored in answer.
Entering yes makes the condition False. The program then displays Ready.
code:
answer = ""
while answer != "yes":
    answer = input("Type yes to finish: ")
print("Ready.")
expectedOutput:
Type yes to finish: no
Type yes to finish: yes
Ready.
initialOutput:
Type yes to finish: no
Type yes to finish: yes
Ready.

title: Controlling a Loop with a Boolean Flag
paragraphs: A Boolean flag stores True or False.
Here, running starts as True. The loop checks that flag before each iteration.
Entering quit changes running to False. The next condition check ends the loop.
expectedOutput:
Command: hello
Command: quit
Loop complete.
initialOutput:
Command: hello
Command: quit
Loop complete.

title: The Current Iteration Finishes
paragraphs: Changing the flag does not jump out of the current code block.
The remaining instructions in that iteration still run.
Here, Iteration complete. is displayed after quit. The next condition check ends the loop.
code:
running = True
while running:
    command = input("Command: ")
    if command == "quit":
        running = False
    print("Iteration complete.")
print("Loop complete.")
expectedOutput:
Command: quit
Iteration complete.
Loop complete.
initialOutput:
Command: quit
Iteration complete.
Loop complete.

title: Wrap Up
bullets: A while loop checks its condition before each iteration.
A True condition starts another iteration.
The loop can run zero times when its first check is False.
Update values in the body so the stopping condition can be reached.
A Boolean flag can be changed to False to end the loop at its next check.
